process_conclusion: The frontier-first selector shows a concrete but bounded advantage over the prior opportunistic queue choice. Frontier-first period: six hypothesis cells closed (short-horizon reversal FALSIFIED 37263008074, cross-sectional relative strength FALSIFIED 37304873966, volatility targeting FALSIFIED 37314710995, momentum SUPPORTED 37318950814, cross-sectional momentum FALSIFIED, 20-day breakout FALSIFIED 37414038601) plus two momentum qualification sweeps (lookback 3/5/10 in 37361000967 and lookback 20/60 in 37394344201), each with a durable artifact, an independent verifier, determinism, and a green regression suite; line 12 records the summary decision as RETAIN (verified), although the per-activation history row for 37318950814 (line 57) still carries a stale UNVERIFIED (process delta) label that the summary supersedes. Opportunistic period: zero closed frontier cells, one documented selection defect (37260572520's objective came from the queued receipt item rather than a frontier cell), and one execution-blocked activation (37261348530) whose cause was a denied bash tool at that layer, i.e. an execution-environment failure that must not be counted against the selector. The queue also tracks resolution correctly (R-004 RESOLVED; R-001 next, matching the frontier's own Next action). The advantage is not absolute: the cross-sectional-momentum cell (63-day lookback) is a one-parameter variant of the already-falsified CSRS cell (20-day lookback) and its falsified verdict was its own a-priori prediction, so one of six hypothesis cells was a near-duplicate. Durable-record defects were also found: no logs/ section exists for three frontier-first activations (37304873966, 37394344201, and the cross-sectional-momentum cell, which additionally has no run id), the only admitted positive cell (momentum) is split across LEARNING_STATE.md lines 30-32 so its status text does not render as a table row, two orphan check scripts (momentum_sweep.py, momentum_hold_period_sensitivity.py) have no artifact or verdict, and selection_basis has a 5-vs-7 arity mismatch. Net: the selector earns RETAIN on selection quality and decisiveness, while the novelty guard and the activation-record layer are the current bottlenecks.
research_conclusion: Research/simulation only; no live trading or production execution, and no claim about live-market profitability. The short-horizon momentum edge is retained under the repository's existing cost model: COST_ROBUST at all three lookbacks (6/10 assets at lookback 3, 5/10 at 5, 5/10 at 10), 16/30 cells COST_ROBUST, median retention 0.99-1.00, and the zero-cost column exactly reproduces momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json for all 10 tickers x 3 lookbacks. The independent verifier reproduces every median, null median, segment list, n_folds, verdict, cost class, and universe verdict. However, the result does not establish conservative-cost robustness: the engine prices every fill at close + slippage, so sell-side slippage is favorable, a slippage-only round trip ends at exactly initial equity for both long and short, and on AMZN the slippage-only total return (+5.539447) slightly exceeds the zero-cost return (+5.537258) while realistic (+5.518392) is essentially commission-only (+5.516203). The 'conservative' grid level therefore does not stress the candidate. MSFT's lookback-5 COST_FRAGILE label is a null-dispersion artifact (candidate medians unchanged to four decimals; null dispersion 0.008121 -> 0.003300), not a cost effect. No claim of conservative-cost robustness is made.
unverified: Causal attribution of post-period throughput to the selector is not identified: the pre-period also lacked executable real-data infrastructure, so selector quality and toolkit maturity are confounded.
